Exhortations to zeal, and constancy in professing the gospel.

was St. Paul from Rome in A.D. 62 or 63. St. Paul's connection with Philippi was of a peculiar character, which gave rise to the writing of this epistle.
Paul

At the end of these two years Felix (q.v.) was succeeded in the governorship of Palestine by Porcius Festus, before whom the apostle was again heard. But judging it right at this crisis to claim the privilege of a Roman citizen, he appealed to the emperor (Acts 25:11).
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle offers up thanksgivings and prayers, for the good work of grace in the Philippians (vv. 1–7); He expresses affection, and prays for them (vv. 8–11); Fortifies them against being cast down at his sufferings (vv. 12–20); He stood prepared for glorifying Christ by life, or death (vv. 21–26); Exhortations to zeal, and constancy in professing the gospel (vv. 27–30). People named: Paul, Timotheus. Places: Philippi.
ch.mh: The highest honour of the most eminent ministers is, to be servants of Christ.
q: Read verses 1–7 (The apostle offers up thanksgivings and prayers, for the good work of grace in the Philippians). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 8–11 (He expresses affection, and prays for them), what do you learn about suffering and endurance?
Verse 6 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside 1 Thessalonians 5:23–24. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Paul’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of faith and trust in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Philippians?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Let us leave it to Christ, which way he will make us serviceable to his glory, whether by labour or suffering, by diligence or patience, by living to his honour in working for him, or dying to his honour in suffering for him.
ch.a: Bring a present hardship to God and memorize the key verse as an anchor.

Epaphroditus

Fair, graceful; belonging to Aphrodite or Venus the messenger who came from Phillipi to the apostle when he was a prisoner at Rome (Phil. 2:25-30; 4:10-18). Paul mentions him in words of esteem and affection.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Exhortations to a kind, humble spirit and behaviour (vv. 1–4); The example of Christ (vv. 5–11); Diligence in the affairs of salvation, and to be examples to the world (vv. 12–18); The apostle's purpose of visiting Philippi (vv. 19–30). People named: Timotheus, Epaphroditus.
ch.mh: Here are further exhortations to Christian duties; to like-mindedness and lowly-mindedness, according to the example of the Lord Jesus.
q: Read verses 1–4 (Exhortations to a kind, humble spirit and behaviour). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?

What does Timotheus’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of hope and restoration in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Philippians?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: The more perverse others are, the more careful we should be to keep ourselves blameless and harmless.
ch.a: Encourage someone who is discouraged with a promise from this chapter.

Benjamin
The tribe of Benjamin at the Exodus was the smallest but one (Num. 1:36, 37; Ps. 68:27). During the march its place was along with Manasseh and Ephraim on the west of the tabernacle.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle cautions the Philippians against judaizing false teachers, and renounces his own former privileges (vv. 1–11); Expresses earnest desire to be found in Christ; also his pressing on toward perfection; and recommends his own example to other believers (vv. 12–21). People named: Benjamin, Hebrews.
ch.mh: Sincere Christians rejoice in Christ Jesus.

bg: philippians, epistle to the
was St. Paul from Rome in A.D. 62 or 63. St. Paul's connection with Philippi was of a peculiar character, which gave rise to the writing of this epistle.
Macedonia
In New Testament times, was a Roman province lying north of Greece. It was governed by a propraetor with the title of proconsul.
Thessalonica
A large and populous city on the Thermaic bay. It was the capital of one of the four Roman districts of Macedonia, and was ruled by a praetor.
Epaphroditus

Fair, graceful; belonging to Aphrodite or Venus the messenger who came from Phillipi to the apostle when he was a prisoner at Rome (Phil. 2:25-30; 4:10-18). Paul mentions him in words of esteem and affection.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle exhorts the Philippians to stand fast in the Lord (vv. 1); Gives directions to some, and to all in general (vv. 2–9); Expresses contentment in every condition of life (vv. 10–19); He concludes with prayer to God the Father, and his usual blessing (vv. 20–23). People named: Epaphroditus, Euodias, Syntyche, Clement, Cesar, Rome. Places: Macedonia, Thessalonica.
ch.mh: The believing hope and prospect of eternal life, should make us steady and constant in our Christian course.
q: Read verses 1 (The apostle exhorts the Philippians to stand fast in the Lord). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 2–9 (Gives directions to some, and to all in general), what do you learn about the church and fellowship?
Verse 13 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Isaiah 41:10. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Epaphroditus’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of worship and praise in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Philippians?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: We should look upon God, under all our weakness and fears, not as an enemy, but as a Father, disposed to pity us and help us.
ch.a: Write down three things this chapter shows about God and thank Him for each.
